name: Inheritance Types, Access Modes, and the Diamond Problem
subject: Object-Oriented Programming Systems

mcqs.question: In C++, how is the Diamond Problem resolved during multiple inheritance?
options: Using the dynamic_cast operator in the derived class
By inheriting from the common base class using the "virtual" keyword
By declaring all member functions in the common base as inline
By marking the common base class with the final keyword
mcqs.explanation: Virtual inheritance (class B : virtual public A) ensures that only one shared subobject of class A exists in any derived class hierarchy.

mcqs.question: Given class Base and class Derived : public Base. In what order do constructors and destructors execute?
options: Constructor: Base then Derived; Destructor: Derived then Base
Constructor: Derived then Base; Destructor: Base then Derived
Constructor: Base then Derived; Destructor: Base then Derived
Constructor: Derived then Base; Destructor: Derived then Base
mcqs.explanation: Base class is constructed first to establish foundational state before derived construction. Destructors execute in reverse (Derived cleanup first, then Base).

mcqs.question: Under private inheritance in C++ (class Derived : private Base), what happens to public members of Base?
options: They are completely erased and cannot be called by Derived members
mcqs.explanation: In private inheritance, all public and protected members of the base class become private members of the derived class.
